chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Abdullah ibn Aamir, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad al-Hashimy, from Abu Hafs al-Attar, a Sheikh from the people of Medina, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whenever one of you prays the Prescribed Salat and exits from the Masjid, so let him pause by the door, then let him say, O Allah! You Called me, so I answered Your Call, and I prayed the Prescribed Salat, and I spread out in Your earth just as You Commanded me. So I ask You from Your Grace, the working in Your obedience, and keeping aside from Your Anger, and sufficiency of the sustenance by Your Mercy.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite when leaving the mosque after prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of al-Kulayni in *Al-Kafi*, emphasizes the spiritual transition from the sacred space of the mosque to the worldly realm by pausing at the threshold to offer a concise du'a. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on maintaining mindfulness (muraqabah) and gratitude for divine acceptance, linking the physical act of exiting with a request for sustained obedience and sufficiency (al-kaaf) in daily life. The supplication serves as a bridge between ritual worship and worldly conduct, ensuring that the believer's engagement with creation remains aligned with divine command.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Abdullah Bin Aamir, from Ali Bin Mahziyar, from Ja’far Bin Muhammad Al Hashimy, from Abu Hafs Al Attar, a Sheykh from the people of Al Medina who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘Rasool-Allahsaww said: ‘Whenever one of you prays the Prescribed Salāt and exits from the Masjid, so let him pause by the door, then let him say, ‘O Allahazwj! Youazwj Called me, so I answered Yourazwj Call, and I prayed the Prescribed Salāts, and I spread out in spread out in Yourazwj earth just as Youazwj Commanded me. So I ask Youazwj from Yourazwj Grace, the working in Yourazwj obedience, and keeping aside from Yourazwj Anger, and sufficiency of the sustenance by Yourazwj Mercy’.
en.sarwar: 4. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Amir from Ali ibn Mahziyar from Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Hashimiy from abu Hafs al-‘Attar -Shaykh of the people of Madinah who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say. ‘The Messenger of Allah has said, “When any one of you after completing an obligatory Salah (prayer), wants to leave a Masjid he should stand at the door and say, ‘O Lord You called me and I answered Your call. I performed my obligatory Salah (prayer). I want to move in Your land as You have commanded me. Now I ask You to help me to act in Your obedience, avoid making You angry with me and suffice me in matters of my sustenance through Your mercy.”””
